title: Canary Phase Checkpoints — Non-linear Undo & Audit Trail Panel
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Operators need a compact way to inspect, pause, and reverse individual canary phases without stepping backward through a linear timeline. Current timeline-first flows make it hard to compare the exact traffic snapshot, assertions, and metadata that existed at an earlier phase.

Goal: Design a lightweight panel that surfaces immutable "checkpoints" for each canary phase. Each checkpoint captures: traffic split, active assertions (metric guards), routing variant IDs, a short rationale, and a pointer to telemetry anchors. The panel supports non-linear undo (restore a single checkpoint), a time-diff view between two checkpoints, and an audit trail that records who restored or edited checkpoints. We want to make rollbacks safer and more discoverable while preserving regulatory auditability for enterprise customers.

Scope: UI/UX flows and low-fidelity prototypes for the Console Rollouts page. Deliverables include: panel wireframes, microcopy for restoration confirmation, a two-state diff visualization (side-by-side/current vs selected), and accessibility-focused keyboard shortcuts for power users. Not in scope: backend storage format and long-term retention policy (handled by Engineering and Compliance).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Panel mock exists in Figma with at least three variants (collapsed list, full details, diff mode).
2) Microcopy reviewed with Legal and PM for audit/regulatory wording.
3) Prototype allows simulated 'restore checkpoint' interactions and shows a stubbed telemetry link.
4) Interaction spec includes keyboard shortcuts and aria labels.
5) Design passes a 5-person moderated usability check (task success >= 80%).
